Order
The petitioner, who was the 1st accused in C.C.No.600 of 2018 on the files of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Ernakulam, was convicted and sentenced by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate for the commission of the offence under Section 498A IPC.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He took up the matter in appeal, by filing Crl.A.No.138 of 2024 before the Additional Sessions Court - V, Ernakulam.
During the pendency of the above appeal, the case was referred for mediation at the instance of the ADR Centre, Ernakulam.
After successful completion of the process of mediation, the Mediator filed a report, along with the Memorandum of Agreement signed by the parties, regarding the terms of settlement between them.

As per condition No.(4) of the terms and conditions of the aforesaid agreement, it was agreed that the parties shall close the entire matters pending 2025:KER:59723 before various courts in connection with their matrimonial issues.
It was further undertaken that necessary steps will be taken to quash all further proceedings pursuant to Crl.A.No.138 of 2024 pending before the Additional Sessions Court - V, Ernakulam.

In page No.2 of the above Memorandum of Agreement, it is stated that the parties have discussed the entire matters pertaining to Crl.A.No.138 of 2024, which arose out of C.C.No.600 of 2018 on the files of the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Ernakulam, and agreed to settle the said case.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the defacto complainant and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

3. Annexure 2 - Memorandum of Agreement of mediation signed by the defacto complainant and the petitioner herein and their respective counsel, would reveal that all the issues which arose out of the marital discord between them have been amicably settled, and that it was specifically undertaken to do the needful to quash the proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.600 of 2018,
which 2025:KER:59723 eventually resulted in Crl.A.No.138 of 2024 after the conviction and sentence awarded upon the petitioner.

The learned counsel for the defacto complainant / 2nd respondent submitted that the defacto complainant is not having any subsisting grievance, and that Majeed Roshan.V.K vs State Of Kerala on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11961554/

sentences.text: since the issue has been amicably settled in mediation, there is no need for enforcing the conviction and sentence awarded upon the petitioner.

Having regard to the fact that the issue involved in this case is purely private in nature, and the parties have sorted out the disputes between them and opted for an amicable settlement in mediation, the enforcement of the conviction and sentence awarded upon the petitioner is totally unnecessary.

For maintaining the harmonious relationship between the parties and also for honouring the sanctity of the mediation agreement, it is highly necessary that the conviction and sentence imposed by the Trial Court upon the petitioner, are to be quashed.

In the result, the petition stands allowed as follows :-
2025:KER:59723

(i) The conviction and sentence awarded by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Ernakulam, upon the petitioner as per the judgment dated 27.02.2024 in C.C.No.600 of 2018, are hereby quashed.

(ii) The Appellate Court dealing with the appeal preferred against the aforesaid judgment, shall close the proceedings, taking note of the above order of this Court.
